…pervading all; by light of various colors all the world-systems are seen as like emanations, illusions, rainbows, mirages, the moon in water, and reflections. From that utpala arises Tārā, blue, with two arms, the right holding a triśūla, the left hand holding an utpala with its stem; her beautiful body adorned with jewel necklaces, earrings, armlets, and ornaments of various kinds; in the full bloom of youth; with a smiling face; seated in the even cross-legged posture upon moon and lotus. To the south, upon moon and lotus, from a yellow utpala arisen from RE together with its seed syllable, pervading all the world-systems, by light of various colors all the world-systems are seen as like emanations, illusions, rainbows, mirages, the moon in water, and reflections. From that utpala arises Tārā, her body the color of refined gold, with two arms, the right holding a sword, the left holding an utpala with its stem; her beautiful body adorned with jewel necklaces, earrings, armlets, and various ornaments; in the full bloom of youth; with a slightly smiling face; in the even cross-legged posture; seated upon moon and lotus. To the west, upon moon and lotus

…seat, seated upon moon and lotus. At the eastern gate, upon moon and lotus, from an utpala arisen from TAṂ together with its seed syllable, light of various colors pervades all the world-systems, and all the world-systems are seen as like emanations, illusions, rainbows, mirages, the moon in water, and reflections. From that utpala arises Tārā of the Hook, her body white, with two arms holding a hook; her wrathful body adorned with jewel necklaces, earrings, armlets, and ornaments of various kinds; in the full bloom of youth; with a slightly wrathful face; abiding with legs extended and drawn in upon moon and lotus. At the southern gate, upon lotus and moon, from an utpala arisen from RE together with its seed syllable, light of various colors pervades all the world-systems, and all the world-systems are seen as like emanations, illusions, rainbows, mirages, the moon in water, and reflections. From that utpala arises Tārā of the Noose, her body yellow, with two arms holding a noose; her wrathful body adorned with jewel necklaces, earrings, armlets, and ornaments of various kinds; in the full bloom of youth, adorned with various kinds, in the full bloom of youth; with a slightly wrathful face; abiding with legs extended and drawn in upon moon and lotus.
